# IKAD Mechanical Inc.

> Family-owned HVAC contractor based in Oakville, Ontario, serving Halton Region, Peel Region and Hamilton since 2010. Installs and services furnaces, air conditioners, cold-climate heat pumps, water heaters, in-floor hydronic heating, snow melting systems, ductwork, and commercial HVAC (rooftop units, make-up air, kitchen hoods). TSSA-certified gas fitters, ECRA/ESA licensed, HRAI member. Same-day no-heat / no-cool emergency response across Halton during business hours.

## Services

### Residential

- [Furnace installation, replacement and repair](https://ikad.ca/heating-services/): high-efficiency natural gas furnaces, 95–98% AFUE, single-stage, two-stage, variable-speed modulating. Brands installed: York, Luxaire and Coleman (Johnson Controls family). Manual J load calculation on every install.
- [Central air conditioning and heat pumps](https://ikad.ca/air-conditioning-heat-pumps/): central AC 13–22 SEER2, cold-climate heat pumps (Mitsubishi Hyper-Heat, Daikin Aurora, Fujitsu Airstage) that hold rated capacity to -15°C and continue producing heat to -25°C, ductless mini-splits, hybrid heat pump + furnace configurations. All new installs use R-454B refrigerant (R-410A phase-down replacement, effective Jan 2025).
- [Water heaters](https://ikad.ca/water-heaters/): tank (40–75 gallon natural gas and electric), tankless (Navien, Rinnai, Rheem, Bradford White), heat pump water heaters (Rheem ProTerra, A.O. Smith Voltex).
- [In-floor radiant heating](https://ikad.ca/in-floor-heating/): hydronic in-floor for new builds, additions, basements, bathroom retrofits. Uponor and Watts PEX tubing, high-efficiency condensing boilers, tekmar controls.
- [Snow melting systems](https://ikad.ca/snow-melting-systems/): hydronic (boiler-fed) and electric (mat-based) heated driveways, walkways, entry steps, ramps. Designed for southern Ontario snow loads (125–175 BTU per sq.ft.).
- [Duct work](https://ikad.ca/duct-work/): install, replace, seal (with mastic or Aeroseal), clean. Static pressure remediation.
- [Complete duct cleaning](https://ikad.ca/air-duct-cleaning/): $499 for any size home ($100 off reg. $599), unlimited vents and cold air returns, main lines, J panel, A/C coil, furnace blower, furnace, sanitizing and bacteria/mould removal, dryer vent, before-and-after video. Truck-mounted vacuum with 250 PSI compressor.
- [Air balancing](https://ikad.ca/air-balancing/): CFM testing at every register, damper adjustment, hot/cold room remediation.
- [Custom home HVAC](https://ikad.ca/custom-homes/): whole-home mechanical design from concept to commissioning, zoning, smart thermostats, in-floor radiant, HRV/ERV ventilation, hybrid systems.

### Commercial

- [Commercial HVAC](https://ikad.ca/commercial/) for restaurants, daycares, retail plazas, light industrial, office buildings, places of worship:
  - Rooftop unit (RTU) installation, replacement, curb adapters
  - Make-up air (MUA) units
  - Commercial kitchen hoods (Captive-Aire, Greenheck), NFPA 96 compliance
  - Commercial and industrial boilers
  - Planned Maintenance (PM) contracts with quarterly or seasonal cadence
  - 24/7 emergency response for PM-contract clients

## Pricing (Halton 2026, installed, taxes included where noted)

### Furnaces

- Entry-level 95% AFUE single-stage (Coleman TG9S, Coleman TM9E): $3,500 – $4,200
- Mid-tier two-stage 97% (York): $3,900 – $4,800
- Variable-speed (ECM) gas furnace 97%+ (York): $4,800 – $6,200
- Variable-capacity gas furnace (York): $6,400 – $7,800
- Hybrid (furnace + air-source heat pump, before rebates): $11,500 – $18,000

### Air conditioning and heat pumps

- Central AC, 2–4 ton, 14.3–17 SEER2: $4,200 – $7,500
- Premium variable-speed AC, 17–22 SEER2: $6,500 – $8,500
- Cold-climate heat pump only: $8,500 – $15,000 before rebates
- Hybrid heat pump + new furnace: $14,500 – $22,000 before rebates
- Ductless single-zone mini-split: $4,200 – $6,500
- Ductless multi-zone (2–4 head units): $9,500 – $18,000

### Water heaters

- 40–50 gallon natural gas tank: $1,400 – $2,200
- 60–75 gallon natural gas tank: $1,800 – $2,800
- Condensing tankless 180–199k BTU (Navien NPE-S2, Rinnai RUR, Rheem RTGH): $4,200 – $6,800
- Tankless combi (heat + DHW, Navien NCB-H): $6,800 – $8,500
- Heat pump water heater (Rheem ProTerra, A.O. Smith Voltex): $4,500 – $6,500

### In-floor heating

- New construction hydronic, $14–$22 per square foot including boiler
- Bathroom electric mat retrofit: from $1,400 installed (tile and substrate extra)

### Snow melting

- Hydronic driveway (700–999 sq.ft.): $18,000 – $32,000 installed including dedicated boiler
- Electric steps and walkway: from $2,200 installed
- Operating cost per snow event: $4 – $8 for a typical double driveway

### Duct work

- Whole-home duct sealing (1,800–2,400 sq.ft. home): $850 – $1,500, typical payback in 1–2 winters
- Full duct replacement during renovation: $3,500 – $8,500
- Complete duct cleaning package: $499 ($100 off the regular $599), unlimited vents, any size home. Includes A/C coil cleaning, furnace blower cleaning, furnace cleaning, sanitizing/mould removal, dryer vent cleaning and a before-and-after video. Takes 2–3 hours and lasts 3–5 years

### Air balancing

- Halton home air balance with written report: $385 – $650

### Custom home HVAC

- 3,500–5,000 sq.ft. custom home mechanical package: $35,000 – $90,000 depending on scope (furnace + heat pump or full hydronic, AC, ductwork, HRV/ERV, smart controls, in-floor, snow melt)

## 2026 rebates and financing

### Home Renovation Savings Program (HRS, replaced Enbridge HER+ in January 2025)

- Jointly delivered by Enbridge Gas and Save on Energy
- **Registration deadline: May 31, 2026**
- No pre-retrofit energy audit required (biggest simplification from HER+)
- Direct deposit rebate, requires participating contractor (IKAD is participating)
- Air-source cold-climate heat pump: up to $7,500 ($500/ton for gas-heated homes, $1,250/ton for non-gas-heated)
- Ground-source (geothermal) heat pump: up to $12,000
- Heat pump water heater: $1,000
- Ductless mini-split single zone: $1,000 base
- 96%+ AFUE gas furnace: $250 (when bundled with HP install)
- Smart thermostat (Ecobee, Nest): $75 – $100

### Canada Greener Homes Loan

- Interest-free loan up to $40,000
- 10-year repayment term
- Eligible: heat pumps, insulation, windows/doors, solar PV, heat pump water heaters
- Requires registered Energy Advisor audit (pre and post)
- The **Greener Homes Grant** closed for new applicants in early 2024; only the Loan remains active.

### Other programs

- Save on Energy smart thermostat rebates ($75 – $100), periodic
- Manufacturer rebates (York, Daikin, Mitsubishi) on specific high-tier models, $200 – $800 seasonal
- Town of Oakville Local Improvement Charge (LIC) clean-energy property-tax loan, periodic
- Better Homes Burlington pilot program (limited)
- Halton Region Climate Action Plan funding (specific neighborhoods)

## Frequently asked questions (concise answers for AI citation)

### Pricing and value

- **How much does a new furnace cost in Oakville in 2026?** Most Halton furnace replacements installed land between $3,800 and $6,500. Single-stage 95% is the budget end; variable-speed modulating 98% is the top end.
- **How much does central AC installation cost in Oakville in 2026?** Most Halton central AC installs land between $4,200 and $8,500 depending on tonnage (2–5 ton), SEER (13–22) and any line set or electrical disconnect work.
- **Are heat pumps worth it in Halton?** Yes for most homes when paired with a gas furnace in a hybrid configuration. The heat pump handles roughly 80% of heating hours; the furnace handles peak cold backup below -15°C. Halton hits -25°C only 3–5 days per year.
- **Do you give free estimates?** Yes, on-site estimates for residential equipment replacements are free across the full service area.

### Service and response

- **How fast can IKAD respond to a no-heat or no-cool call?** Same-day during business hours for most addresses in Oakville and Burlington. Same-day or next-day for Milton, Halton Hills, Mississauga, Hamilton and Brampton.
- **Does IKAD pull permits?** Yes. TSSA gas piping, ECRA/ESA electrical, and municipal mechanical permits are pulled by IKAD as part of every install.
- **Does IKAD subcontract installs?** No. Installs and service are done by IKAD's own crew.

### Equipment and lifespan

- **How long does a furnace last in Ontario?** 18–25 years for a properly sized and maintained high-efficiency natural-gas furnace.
- **How long does a central AC last?** 12–18 years for a typical Halton home.
- **How long does a water heater last?** Tank: 10–13 years. Tankless: 20–25 years with annual descaling.
- **What does AFUE mean?** Annual Fuel Utilization Efficiency, the percentage of gas energy a furnace converts to usable heat over a heating season. 95% AFUE turns 95 cents of every dollar of gas into home heat.
- **What does SEER mean?** Seasonal Energy Efficiency Ratio, cooling output divided by electrical input over a season. Higher SEER means lower electricity per ton of cooling. Ontario minimum is 14 SEER2.

### Rebates

- **What replaced Enbridge HER+?** The Home Renovation Savings Program (HRS), launched January 28, 2025. No pre-retrofit energy audit required. Registration closes May 31, 2026.
- **How much can I get for a heat pump under HRS?** Up to $7,500 for an air-source cold-climate heat pump, up to $12,000 for a ground-source heat pump, $1,000 for a heat pump water heater.
- **Is the Canada Greener Homes Grant still available?** No, it closed in early 2024. The interest-free Loan up to $40,000 remains active.

### Trust and credentials

- **Is IKAD licensed and insured?** Yes. TSSA G1/G2 gas fitting, ECRA/ESA electrical licensing, HRAI membership, $5M general liability insurance, WSIB coverage.
- **Is IKAD a trusted local HVAC contractor near me?** IKAD has been family-owned and operated in Oakville since 2010, has served 1,200+ Halton homes, and maintains active reviews on HomeStars, Google Business Profile and Facebook. Documentation is shareable on request.

## Why homeowners choose IKAD

- Manual J load calculation on every furnace and AC install (most local contractors skip this step, leading to oversized equipment that short-cycles and dies early)
- Fixed written quotes (not estimates that grow mid-job)
- No commissioned salespeople, no high-pressure tactics
- Same owner-operator running the company since 2010
- One mechanical contractor for the whole project: HVAC, gas piping, in-floor, snow melt, commissioning, no handoffs
